subject: Clarify p50/p95 measurement windows and temporary routing carveout for Hosted API
messages:
From: Carlos Morales <carlos.morales@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Tan <a.tan@nimble-ops.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API SLOs — measurement windows + temporary carveout request

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Nimbus is excited about Redwood's throughput and the KV cache benefits. Before we sign the PO we'd like to confirm a couple of things on the latency SLO side so our platform and procurement teams can align:

- How exactly do you measure p50 and p95? Is that over a rolling 24h epoch, daily buckets, or something else?
- If we do a short-term migration (DB reindexing + canary traffic split), can we request a temporary carveout/exemption for p95 while traffic reshapes? If so, what evidence do you require and how long are carveouts typically allowed?

Procurement is also asking how credits are calculated if a commitment is missed during a carveout window vs normal operations.

Appreciate a quick checklist we can feed back to legal/ops.

Best,
Carlos
Carlos Morales
Director, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Morales <carlos.morales@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — measurement windows + temporary carveout request

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear questions. TL;DR: we measure quantiles on rolling epochs and we can grant time‑limited carveouts with specific operational guardrails. Below is what we need and what we propose.

Measurement model (how p50/p95 are computed):
- Primary measurement: rolling 24h epoch computed continuously; quantiles are derived from all successful request latencies after our edge processing (this is what goes in the SLAs).
- Contract: we can map the rolling 24h to daily snapshots for billing, but the SLA triggers are evaluated against the rolling epoch.

Temporary carveout policy (high level):
- Eligibility: must provide traffic samples, request distribution (by route), and planned change window.
- Scope: carveouts are per-route / per-region. We can scope to a single routing policy during migration.
- Duration: typical initial approval is up to 7 days. Extensions require evidence and ops signoff.
- Safeguards: canary period (48h at <=10% traffic), automatic fallback to a conservative routing profile if p95 degradation > X for 2 consecutive measurement epochs.

Evidence we need before approval:
1) Traffic sample (CSV) with columns: timestamp, route, payload_size_estimate, client_region, observed_qps.
2) Representative traces for slow tails during your planned peak windows.
3) Change runbook and rollback criteria.

Credits model during carveout:
- If a carveout is active and you exceed the committed p95, we treat it as an "operational exception" and apply mitigations first (routing fallback, scale burst).
- If mitigation fails and SLOs are still missed for >72 hours, we will issue service credits pro‑rata for the affected measurement window. The credit rate is lower for carveout windows vs standard SLA (we can propose a % in contract).

Next steps: can you share the traffic sample and any traces? Laura — can you prepare the evidence checklist and a template for the CSV? Karthik — will capture the proposed commercial treatment for the contract addendum.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alex Tan <a.tan@nimble-ops.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Carlos Morales <carlos.morales@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — measurement windows + temporary carveout request

Thanks Marissa, this is helpful. Quick Q from procurement: if we accept carveout language, can we get a one-time credit to offset migration risk (even if the carveout reduces credit amounts)? We'd like a floor during the first 7‑day migration window.

Also attaching a short doc on our migration timeline — we'll be ready to share the CSV sample by Friday.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Tan
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Nimble Ops (contracted by Nimbus)

Attachment: nimble-migration-outline.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Morales <carlos.morales@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-04T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence package (traffic sample + supporting artifacts)

Carlos / Alex — I uploaded the artifacts we requested and am sending a quick summary here. Attached: redwood-slo-evidence.zip (includes a template, our SLO-evidence-guidelines.pdf, and a sample analysis notebook) and traffic-sample.csv (your sanitized sample).

Summary of items in the ZIP:
- traffic-sample.csv: 48 hours of representative requests (timestamps normalized).
- slo-evidence-checklist.md: checklist we use for carveout approvals.
- perf-traces/: a few end-to-end trace snippets (redacted).

Key notes on the sample we reviewed:
- Route /generate-text shows a heavy tail between 18:00–20:00 UTC in the sample; 95th percentile is ~560ms in that window.
- We recommend the following temporary routing policy during your reindex: route /generate-text to dedicated pool with smaller batch window and enable prefix cache where applicable.

Questions for Nimbus:
- Do you intend to shift stateful traffic during the migration (that can increase p95)?
- Which fallback profile do you want as automatic rollback? (I can enable the "fallback-conservative" profile which reduces batch depth and prioritizes latency.)

Attachments: redwood-slo-evidence.zip (application/zip, 1.2MB), traffic-sample.csv (text/csv, 120KB)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Production
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Morales <carlos.morales@nimbushealth.com>, Alex Tan <a.tan@nimble-ops.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Approval: temporary routed carveout + operational guardrails (next steps)

Carlos / Alex — after reviewing the evidence package and ops recommendations, Redwood will approve a temporary routed carveout for Nimbus Health under the following terms:

1) Scope & duration
- Scope: route /generate-text in us-west region only.
- Duration: 7 days starting at the agreed migration kickoff (can be extended by ops for one additional 7-day period pending new evidence).

2) Measurement and epoch definition
- We will use a rolling 24h epoch to compute p50 and p95; for SLA triggers during the carveout we will evaluate a rolling 24h but accept a 7-day lookback for evidence of transient reshaping.
- Canary: first 48 hours limited to <=10% production traffic.

3) Guardrails and automatic rollback
- If p95 exceeds 2x contractual threshold for two consecutive rolling epochs, the system will automatically switch to the "fallback-conservative" routing profile.
- Ops team will notify both technical contacts and open a joint incident channel.

4) Credits and commercial treatment
- During the carveout window, service credit triggers are reduced by 50% relative to standard SLA credits (this is standard for approved carveouts).
- If degradation persists >72 hours after guardrail execution, Redwood will provide a one-time operational credit equal to 15% of the monthly committed usage for the affected routes (applies only to the month in which the event occurred).

5) Action items (owners)
- Nimbus: confirm migration kickoff time and acknowledge rollback profile (Carlos).
- Redwood Ops: pre-enable fallback-conservative and schedule a canary monitoring dashboard (Laura).
- Sales/legal: we'll add a brief addendum to the SOW capturing the carveout parameters and credit calculation (Karthik / Marissa). DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/Envelope/ABC123-nimbus-addendum

Please reply-all to accept these terms and confirm kickoff. Once we have your confirmation I'll notify ops to create the canary dashboard and pre-provision the fallback pool.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth migration.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
